title: Torts
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Analyze intentional torts and their defenses, negligence (duty, breach, causation and damages), comparative fault and assumption of risk, strict liability, products liability, nuisance, defamation and privacy, and vicarious liability.

weeks.2: Trespass, conversion and intentional infliction of emotional distress
weeks.4: Negligence: duty and the standard of care
weeks.8: Defenses: contributory and comparative fault, assumption of risk

blocks.deliverable: Identify the intentional torts in five fact patterns.
Apply the reasonable-person standard and negligence per se.
Analyze causation in a multiple-defendant problem.
Week 7 midterm; compute recovery under pure and modified comparative fault.
Analyze a design-defect claim under the consumer-expectation and risk-utility tests.
Write an IRAC answer to a defamation problem involving a public figure.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Tort memo and complaint: from a supplied accident file, write a 2,000-word office memo on every plausible claim and defense, then draft the negligence count of a complaint.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
